Sweet Sticky Rice with Fruit

Served at: Buddhist Ghost Festival (Ullambana)

Serves 4Prep 15 minCook 30 min

Sweet Sticky Rice with Fruit is a traditional offering during the Buddhist Ghost Festival, also known as Ullambana. This dish is often prepared as a respectful and nourishing food to honor ancestors and spirits, symbolizing gratitude and compassion.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup glutinous (sticky) rice (200 g)
  • 1 1/2 cups water (360 ml)
  • 1/2 cup coconut milk (120 ml)
  • 1/4 cup sugar (50 g)
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1 ripe mango, peeled and sliced
  • 1/2 cup fresh lychee or longan, peeled and pitted
  • 1 tablespoon toasted sesame seeds

Method

  1. Rinse the sticky rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak it in water for at least 1 hour (or overnight if possible).
  2. Drain the soaked rice and place it in a steamer lined with cheesecloth or a clean kitchen towel.
  3. Steam the rice over boiling water for about 20-25 minutes until tender and translucent.
  4. While the rice is steaming, combine coconut milk, sugar, and salt in a small saucepan and warm over low heat until sugar dissolves. Do not boil.
  5. Transfer the cooked sticky rice to a bowl and gently fold in the sweetened coconut milk mixture until well combined.
  6. Serve the sticky rice warm or at room temperature, topped with sliced mango and fresh lychee or longan.
  7. Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds over the top for added flavor and texture.

Tips

  • If fresh lychee or longan is unavailable, canned versions can be used after draining.
  • For a vegan version, ensure the sugar is vegan-friendly and use coconut sugar as a substitute if desired.
  • This dish can also be served chilled for a refreshing variation during warmer months.
